# **Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding**: zero documented flow from signup → first class → habit formation (discovery call? induction protocol? buddy system? goal-setting session?)
- **Churn & Win-back**: no systematic approach to pause requests, cancellations, or re-engagement campaigns—likely losing members by default
- **Coaching Development & Quality Assurance**: no structured path for coach progression, feedback loops, or class quality standards (Class Quality Audit exists as gap but sits orphaned without coaching SOP)
- **Member Check-ins & Retention Cadence**: no defined touchpoints post-onboarding (week 2? month 1? quarterly?) to prevent silent churn
- **GDPR & Data Privacy**: compliance risk if handling member data without documented process
- **Referral Programme Operations**: no mechanics, tracking, or incentive fulfillment process
- **Incident & Complaint Handling**: no protocol for member injuries, safety issues, or complaints escalation
- **Finance & Billing**: no SOP for membership billing, payment failures, refunds, or financial reconciliation
- **Health & Safety Incident Log**: no documented response to accidents, near-misses, or safeguarding concerns

---

# **Needs updating**

- **Clients (28/37)**: Likely missing outcome-tracking, milestone celebrations, and 1:1 goal review cadence—these drive retention and upsell in boutique fitness
- **Coaches (21/24)**: Weekly key tasks SOP missing—leaves ambiguity on session prep, member notes, class debrief; no coaching development roadmap = no clear career path or upskilling route
- **General (1/1)**: Only 1 SOP in General is a red flag—probably needs: brand voice/tone, crisis comms, staff handbook essentials, decision-making

# Service Menu Build — Execution for The Forge

• **Start with your revenue reality, not your dreams.** Pull last month's actual bookings/sales data. Map what members actually buy (classes, PT sessions, packages, add-ons). This becomes your "what we offer" — base it on what sells, not what you think should sell. Cut anything with zero traction in the last 60 days.

• **Build TWO menus, not one.** Coach menu = simplified internal version showing them what sells, commission/rates, and upsell opportunities (e.g., "members doing 2 classes/week are 70% more likely to add one PT session"). Member menu = beautiful, clear pricing with one anchor price per service tier. Remove decision paralysis — no more than 3 package options per category.

• **Embed price anchoring strategically.** Put your highest-priced PT package or premium membership first on the member menu. This makes everything else look reasonable. For coaches: show them the member price + what they earn. Transparency kills objection.

• **Lock this into operations TODAY.** Photograph the finalized menus, send to all coaches via WhatsApp with a 5-min chat about any questions (not a meeting). Upload final version to your website, socials, and print 10 copies for your reception desk. Don't overthink — version 1.0 is done in 48 hours, you refine it in 90 days based on what actually sells.

• **Use this as your sales script baseline.** Every new inquiry gets the same menu framework. Your admin/coaches stop making up prices on the fly. Track which service sells fastest — that's your next growth lever.

# The Forge — Fractional CFO Actions

## REVENUE — URGENT: Member Quality Collapse

• **Your Rev/member has crashed 29% in 2 months** (£137 in Sept → £103 in Oct). Simultaneously, active members rose 11 (Sept to Oct) but revenue *fell* £4.2k. This is classic low-value sign-ups drowning out premium members. **Action: Suspend discount/intro offers immediately; audit Oct intake—are you onboarding at £50/month when Sept baseline was £180/head?** Run a 7-day win-back campaign on Sept cohort (churn was normal at 6.2%) before October leakage accelerates.

• **Churn spiked to 12.8% in May**, then stabilised 3–6%. Oct at 3.9% is *good*, but Sept's 6.2% suggests member satisfaction dipped mid-cycle. **Action: Pull NPS/feedback from Sept joiners within 14 days; tighten onboarding experience (first 2 weeks retention is your churn control valve).** Losing members only hurts if you've paid acquisition cost.

• **Last 3 months (Aug–Oct) average £18.6k revenue vs prior 3 (May–Jul) £17.5k—only +6.3% on flat-to-rising member count (127→172).** You're adding bodies, not value. **Action: Tier your membership (Core £49/m + Premium £79/m with studio hire/PT credits); immediately test a £15/month upsell (class pass 10-pack, retail £80, cost £8 to deliver).** Target: lift Rev/member back to £125 by Dec.

---

## EXPENSES — Where are they? You're hiding margin.

• **You've given me revenue but no P&L.** On £16–22k monthly revenue, I need to see: staff wages, rent/studio costs, software (TeamUp, GoCardless, Stripe fees ~2%), utilities. **Action: Export your Starling P&L by cost centre (or build one). Once I see fixed costs, I'll identify if studio relocation lifted rent burden—if rent jumped >20% with +35 members (Apr→Oct), it's a drag.** Rule of thumb: staffing should be 35–40% of revenue; rent 20–25%. If you're at 60%+ combined, cost base is killing profit.
